d.d: A Central American plant, Agave sisalana, cultivated for its sword-shaped leaves that yield fibers used for rope.
A daughter of the same parents as another person; a female sibling.
d.x: My sister is always driving me crazy.

d.d: A female member of a religious order; especially one devoted to more active service; (informal) a nun.
d.x: Michelle left behind her bank job and became a sister at the local convent.

d.d: Any butterfly in the genus Adelpha, so named for the resemblance of the dark-colored wings to the black habit traditionally worn by nuns.
To strengthen (a supporting beam) by fastening a second beam alongside it.
d.x: I’m trying to correct my sagging floor by sistering the joists.

d.d: The state, or kinship of being sisters.
The quality of being sisterly; sisterly companionship; especially, the sense that women have of being in solidarity with one another.
In the manner of a sister, behaving as one would expect of a sister; as a sister, as sisters.
third-person singular simple present indicative of sister
Of or pertaining to Pope Sixtus.
d.x: The Sistine chapel was built by Pope Sixtus IV.

d.d: Strength of will in the face of adversity; grit, perseverance or determination, regarded as an integral part of Finnish culture.
